note: The earliest located view of 1816, engraved the year after the house was built (1873). From the walk south-east of it, the same side the undated photograph (chicagology_1816_henderson_photo) is taken from, it shows a Second Empire house of two tall storeys over a raised basement under a slated mansard: the south flank in shadow (the engraver's convention for the turned face) with one light on its upper storey only and a canted bay near its rear carried up into a mansard of its own with a dormer, a tall stack rising from the flank's cornice up the main mansard's south face, a bracketed cornice round both faces, three pedimented dormers in the street face, the entrance under a bracketed entablature on pilasters with a stoop down to the east between solid parapets, and the rear range beyond the flank bay, lower than the house, under a moulded cornice. It draws the main mansard as one continuous roof: no raised crown over the front's south end, no cresting, no balcony railing over the entrance, and no fence on the street line, where the later photograph shows each. The street front between the corner and the entrance is hidden behind a parkway tree. The camera is solved from the 1911 sheet's plan points, so each height read off it is a measurement through that solve.
what_it_supplies: the rear range's height and its upper storey's lights, the only picture of it

the south flank's single upper-storey light and its canted bay's mansard and dormer, against the photograph's
the south stack's place on the flank
